offense_analyst.prose: CLE is a run-leaning early-down team that turns pass-heavy in obvious passing spots: it throws on 59.7% of early downs [oc1] over 464 plays [oc2], and on 3rd-and-long it drops back 96.2% of the time [oc3] over 52 plays [oc4]. That is the shift to force, so LV's pass rush and disguise should be ready for 3rd-and-8-plus. CLE's pass rate over expected on early downs is +1.5 points [oc5], 9th in the league [oc6], so it leans pass more than the situation predicts. Its passing efficiency is only average: pass EPA per play is -0.01 [oc7], 22nd in the league [oc8]. Judkins takes 58.9% of rushes [oc9] over 214 rushes [oc10], so the run game is mostly one back. The targets spread across Concepcion (19.9% [oc11]), Boston (19.6% [oc12]) and Fannin (19.6% [oc13]), with Jeudy at 10.1% [oc14] over 316 targets [oc15]. No single receiver dominates, so LV cannot take away one primary target. CLE uses motion on 58.8% of plays [oc16], play action on 17.1% of dropbacks [oc17], screens on 11.1% [oc18] and RPOs on 6.1% of plays [oc19]. The shot-play profile is modest: average depth of target is 7.0 yards [oc20] and explosive pass plays are 8.8% [oc21]. LV's defense is the vulnerable side: it allows -0.17 EPA per pass play, ranked 30th of 32 [oc22], with a sack rate of 6.2% [oc23] and a pressure proxy of 16.0% [oc24] on 374 dropbacks [oc25]. Game plan: stress LV's coverage with motion and play-action off early-down runs, and expect CLE to attack LV's weak pass defense with quick throws to a rotating trio.
